statement_record.book: If C is a small and complete category and U : C ⟶ X preserves all limits, then U has a left adjoint; smallness of C makes the solution-set condition of the AFT automatic, because the objects of C already form a set.
statement_record.intree: Theorem GAFT {C D : Category} (U : C ⟶ D) (comp : @Complete C) (cont : @PreservesImageLimit C D U) (sols : forall d : D, SolutionSet U d) : { F : D ⟶ C & F ⊣ U }.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: GAFT ALWAYS demands an explicit SolutionSet U d at every d, which is exactly the hypothesis Corollary 9.31 claims to eliminate. The library has no smallness predicate on categories at all, so the corollary's hypothesis (C small) cannot even be stated. Two deviations run the other way and are not weakenings: the preservation hypothesis is the cone-level PreservesImageLimit rather than the apex-only PreservesAllLimits (the correct, stronger reading of 'preserves limits', documented in the GAFT.v header), and the conclusion is a genuine packaged left adjoint { F & F ⊣ U }.

gap: The corollary itself (complete + small + limit-preserving ⇒ left adjoint) is not stated anywhere. What is missing is exactly one step: a construction of SolutionSet U d out of smallness of C — concretely sol_index := { c : C & d ~> U c }, sol_obj := projT1, sol_arr := projT2, sol_covers with t := id and factorization by id_left. No such construction, and no notion of a small (or locally small) category, exists in the tree; the only in-tree producer of a SolutionSet is Adjunction/SAFT.v's SAFT_solution_set, which routes through cogenerators and well-powered indexing rather than smallness.

evidence.intree_statement: Definition left_adjoint_preserves_colimits {C D : Category} {F : D ⟶ C} {U : C ⟶ D} (A : F ⊣ U) : PreservesAllColimits F := fun J G => left_adjoint_preserves_colimit A G.

statement_record.book: For complete posets P and Q, a monotone f : P → Q has a right adjoint g : Q → P if and only if f is cocontinuous (preserves all set-indexed joins); the right adjoint is g(q) = ⋁{ x ∈ P : f(x) ≤ q }, verified in both directions. This is the dual AFT applied to a small complete category.
statement_record.intree: Definition left_adjoint_preserves_colimits {C D : Category} {F : D ⟶ C} {U : C ⟶ D} (A : F ⊣ U) : PreservesAllColimits F.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: only the EASY direction is in-tree, and only in its general categorical form (any left adjoint is cocontinuous), never instantiated to posets. The library's thin categories exist (Instance/Proset.v, Instance/Poset.v) but carry no completeness structure, and no lemma identifies a colimit of a discrete diagram in a Proset with a join, so even the easy direction is not available as the book's statement about monotone maps and joins.

gap: The substantive direction — cocontinuous ⇒ a right adjoint exists, with the explicit formula g(q) = ⋁{ x : f(x) ≤ q } and the two-way verification of p ≤ g(q) ⟺ f(p) ≤ q — is entirely absent, as is any notion of a complete poset / complete lattice. Also absent: the identification of (co)limits in Instance/Proset.v with meets/joins, so LAPC cannot be read off as 'f preserves joins' without new work. Instance/Poset.v discusses Galois connections and the poset AFT only in its prose header (lines 60-86); the sole concrete Galois-style adjunction in the tree is Instance/Props.v's (- ∧ P) ⊣ (P → -), a single instance rather than the criterion.

statement_record.book: For C small and complete and any U : C ⟶ Sets, the following are equivalent: (1) U preserves all limits; (2) U has a left adjoint; (3) U is representable. Immediate from Cor 9.31 plus the observation that a left adjoint F ⊣ U gives U ≅ Hom(F1, −).

evidence.intree_statement: Definition SAFT {C D : Category} (U : C ⟶ D) (comp : @Complete C) (cont : @PreservesImageLimit C D U) (G : Cogenerator C) (WP : forall x : C, SubobjectIndex x) (cover : SubobjectCover U comp G WP) : { F : D ⟶ C & F ⊣ U } := GAFT U comp cont (SAFT_solution_set U comp G WP cover).

Lemma cogenerator_canonical_monic {C : Category} (comp : @Complete C) (G : Cogenerator C) (c : C) : Monic (cogen_canonical comp G c).  (the classical 'the canonical map into the power of the cogenerating family is monic' step, proved from cog_separates)

Record Cogenerator {C : Category} := { cog_index : Type; cog_obj : cog_index -> C; cog_separates : forall (x y : C) (f g : x ~> y), (forall (j : cog_index) (k : y ~> cog_obj j), k ∘ f ≈ k ∘ g) -> f ≈ g }.

Record SubobjectIndex {C : Category} (x : C) := { sub_index : Type; sub_dom : sub_index -> C; sub_mono : forall i, sub_dom i ~> x; sub_monic : forall i, Monic (sub_mono i) }.  (well-poweredness of C is then forall x, SubobjectIndex x)

statement_record.book: Let A be locally small and complete, well powered (every object has at most a set of subobjects) and equipped with a cogenerating set {A_i} separating parallel arrows. Then any limit-preserving U : A ⟶ X has a left adjoint. (Proof referred to Mac Lane V.8.)
statement_record.intree: Definition SAFT {C D} (U : C ⟶ D) (comp : @Complete C) (cont : @PreservesImageLimit C D U) (G : Cogenerator C) (WP : forall x : C, SubobjectIndex x) (cover : SubobjectCover U comp G WP) : { F : D ⟶ C & F ⊣ U }.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: SAFT carries one hypothesis the book does not, namely cover : SubobjectCover U comp G WP, which literally ASSERTS the conclusion of the classical image-factorization step (every h : d ~> U c factors as fmap[U] t ∘ s through a well-powered subobject of the cogenerator product). The library derives this from nothing; the header says so explicitly, calling it 'hypothesis-as-data'. Two further deviations: locally-small/smallness is not modelled (cog_index and sub_index are bare Types, so 'set of subobjects' is only a universe-level convention), and the preservation hypothesis is the cone-level PreservesImageLimit (stronger and correct, not a weakening). The genuinely internal mathematics proved here is cogenerator_canonical_monic (separation ⇒ monic).

gap: The image-factorization half of Freyd's SAFT is assumed, not proved: SubobjectCover (Adjunction/SAFT.v:240) is a hypothesis stating exactly that every d-arrow into U c factors through a subobject of ∏_j A_j. Deriving it needs an (epi, mono) factorization in a complete well-powered category, which the tree does not have — Structure/Factorization.v and Structure/Regular/Factorization.v provide OFS/regular-epi-mono factorizations only under their own explicit hypotheses and are never connected to SAFT. Also missing: any smallness notion making 'well powered' a real (rather than data-supplied) condition.

statement_record.book: A finitary equational theory T is finitely many operation symbols with finite arities (0-ary = constants) plus a set of equations between terms; a T-algebra is a set with operations of those arities satisfying the equations; a homomorphism is an underlying function preserving all operations; T-Alg is the category of T-algebras and homomorphisms, with the evident forgetful U : T-Alg ⟶ Sets.
statement_record.intree: OpSignature (operation : Type, arity : operation → Type) + EqSignature (eq, eq_arity, lhs, rhs, naturality) give the theory; Algebra S E is a T-algebra; AlgHom is a homomorphism; Algs : Category is the category of algebras FOR THE SIGNATURE ONLY; on the categorical side Models : Category is the category of models of a LawvereTheory and ev1 : Models T Sets ⟶ Sets is the forgetful functor.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-stronger in one respect and weaker in another. Stronger: arities are arbitrary Types rather than finite, so infinitary theories are covered, and EqSignature imposes lhs/rhs naturality, ruling out non-term-shaped equations. Weaker: the two presentations never meet. Instance/Comp.v's Algs (line 151) has obj := OpAlgebra S, i.e. the EQUATIONS ARE DROPPED — there is no category of Algebra S E — and Algs has no forgetful functor. Conversely Theory/Lawvere's Models/ev1 do deliver T-Alg with its U, but for a LawvereTheory given as an abstract cartesian category, which no in-tree construction produces from a signature-and-equations presentation.

gap: Three precise gaps. (1) No category whose objects are Algebra S E: Instance/Comp.v:151 builds Algs over OpAlgebra S, so the variety cut out by the equations is never made a category (only Product at line 434 shows Algebra S E is closed under products). (2) No forgetful functor out of Algs (or out of any syntactic algebra category) to Coq/Sets; the only forgetful functors of this shape are for fixed varieties, Instance/CMon.v:169 CMon_Forget : CMon ⟶ Sets and Theory/Algebra/Monoid/Hom.v:93 Mon_Forget. (3) No bridge from a syntactic presentation (OpSignature + EqSignature, or a PROP presentation) to a LawvereTheory, so 'the Lawvere theory of T' — and hence 'T-Alg = Models T Sets' for a given equational T — is not available. Finitarity of arities is also not imposed, which is a generalization rather than a defect.

statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker on three counts. (a) Only for theories WITHOUT equations: Free is an OpAlgebra, and there is no free Algebra S E for an EqSignature, so the proposition's actual subject (an equational theory T) is not covered. (b) The universal property is pointwise data, not an adjunction: there is no functor F : Coq ⟶ Algs, no forgetful functor out of Algs, and no F ⊣ U anywhere. (c) It is not obtained from the adjoint functor theorem at all but by an explicit inductive term construction, and its uniqueness proof invokes functional extensionality (Instance/Comp.v:124-131 flags this).
